messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I saw a perf regression comparing the replay harness to the synthetic loadgen after the kernel-selector heuristics change. Replay p95 is ~18% higher on the same commit. Anyone seen this pattern?

Priya: Can you paste the profiler traces (nsys/torch profiler) and the exact load parameters?

Alex: Quick snippets from tonight: ```nsys profile summary:
  select_kernel_gpu: 14.7ms -> 28.2ms
  kv_lookup memcpy: 1.2ms -> 1.8ms
  batching window avg: 3.2ms -> 5.1ms``` Not full traces yet, just what stood out.

Matt: Are both runs on the same GPU/driver/container image? Sometimes tiny driver differences flip kernel choice.

Alex: They were both A100s, driver reported as 525.60 on both, same image tag `redwood-infer:v2026-03-11`. The difference seems tied to request shape distribution — synth uses fixed seq=128 while replay has variable seq (16..2048).

Sarah: That smells like KV cache thrash + batching window variance. When seq tails spike, we can evict or resize caches and kernel-selector may prefer smaller matmul kernels.

Priya: Repro plan: run apples-to-apples — make replay use the synth seq distribution (truncate/pad) and force batching heuristic to fixed window, then compare. Also capture `nsys` full trace and `nvprof --analysis-metrics` for kernel timings.

James: Also check container libcudnn / libnccl minor versions. Run `ldd /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudnn.so` and `nvidia-smi -q | grep "Driver"` on both workers to be 100% sure. Small ABI diffs have bitten us before.

Alex: I did an ldd quick-check: both images report libcudnn 8.4.1, but the replay runner was launched without `--privileged` and had cgroup v2 settings different. Could that affect scheduling preemption? Not sure.

CI-bot: nightly-loadtest: 2101220000 — all green :white_check_mark:

Matt: To narrow changes, bisect kernel-selector commits between v1.12.3 and v1.13.0 with the same replay input. Add a `kernel_choice_histogram` log so we can see which kernels are picked per timestep.

Priya: Also emit KV cache metrics: per-step kv_hit_rate, per-batch active_kv_size, and memcpy bytes. If hit_rate drops on replay tails, that's the smoking gun.

Alex: Short-term action items I’ll run tonight on both T4 and A100:
1) Controlled synth-like replay (fixed seq dist)
2) Native replay (variable seq dist)
3) Force legacy selector: `KERNEL_SELECTOR_MODE=legacy`
4) Capture `nsys` traces + `kernel_choice_histogram` + `kv_hit_rate` logs
I’ll upload traces to the perf bucket and post links.

Sarah: Also include a driver matrix: 525.60 vs 530.30. We saw weird scheduling changes at 530. For each run, toggle `--kernel-flags=sm_80` and `--kernel-flags=sm_90` to watch tile-size selection.

James: If kernel choice flips under thrash to smaller tiles, consider increasing the runtime’s cache buckets or implementing a sticky kernel mapping for repeat shapes to avoid per-step jitter.

Alex: Good suggestions. If I reproduce, next step is a minimal benchmark harness (no replay overhead) that replays the same request sequence but bypasses recording to ensure we isolate runtime selection logic.

Priya: If you can attach the full `nsys` timeline and the `kernel_choice_histogram` we can run the trace-analyzer. I’ll look for memcpy peaks and launch/queue stalls.

Alex: Will do. If anyone wants to pair on the bisect tomorrow at 10:00 PT ping me here. Thanks everyone.
